value: This article defines analog game design as the iterative process of creating and shaping game mechanics, systems, rules, and gameplay, applicable across diverse formats such as board, card, dice, casino, role-playing, and sports games. It details the design process, from initial concept and prototyping to rigorous playtesting and revision, while outlining the distinct roles of designers, developers, and artists. The article further traces the historical evolution of games from ancient folk processes to modern commercial adaptations, influenced by technological advancements, and examines the varied purposes of game design, including entertainment, education, and its study within academia.
